trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Disney World, Orlando, Florida
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.location: 7470 W Irlo Bronson Memorial Hwy, Kissimmee, US (28.3314,-81.5863)

day_by_day.morning: N/A - Late arrival day
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A - Late arrival day
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Orlando International Airport at 22:30 via United Airlines. Take the Magical Express or a budget rideshare (Lyft/Uber ~$25-35) to Ramada by Wyndham Kissimmee Gateway. Check in, unpack, and review your Disney World park tickets and free shuttle schedule posted at the front desk. Pick up any resort maps or discount coupon books available in the lobby.

meals.breakfast: N/A
meals.lunch: N/A
meals.dinner: Grab a quick late-night bite at the hotel vending machines or a nearby 24-hour Walmart Neighborhood Market (~1 mile away) to stock up on snacks, water bottles, and breakfast items for the week — a huge budget saver.

day_by_day.notes: Priority on arrival night: purchase or confirm Disney park tickets online before sleeping to avoid long lines. Download the My Disney Experience app. Set an early alarm for Day 2. Stock your mini-fridge with groceries to cut daily food costs significantly.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up early (6:30 AM) and take the FREE hotel shuttle to Magic Kingdom — aim to arrive at park opening (typically 9:00 AM). Use Early Entry if eligible. Head straight to Tomorrowland and Fantasyland to hit Space Mountain, Seven Dwarfs Mine Train, and Peter Pan's Flight before crowds build. Use the My Disney Experience app to grab Lightning Lane selections strategically.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Liberty Square and Adventureland — ride Pirates of the Caribbean, Haunted Mansion, and Big Thunder Mountain Railroad. Take a midday break during peak heat (1–3 PM) by enjoying the indoor shows like the Hall of Presidents or catching the Festival of Fantasy Parade. Refill your reusable water bottle at any quick-service location for free.
day_by_day.evening: Stay for the iconic Happily Ever After fireworks show (check app for exact time, usually 9:00 PM). Grab a spot on Main Street U.S.A. 30 minutes early for the best view. Take the hotel shuttle back after the show.

meals.breakfast: Eat breakfast at the hotel or from groceries purchased last night — granola bars, fruit, and juice to save money.
meals.lunch: Columbia Harbour House in Liberty Square — try the Lobster Roll or Fried Fish Platter (~$12-15). Split a meal if portions are large.
meals.dinner: Cosmic Ray's Starlight Café in Tomorrowland — one of Magic Kingdom's most affordable quick-service spots. Burgers and chicken meals ~$12-14. Share sides to cut costs.

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable shoes and bring a small backpack with sunscreen, a portable fan, and a refillable water bottle. Magic Kingdom is the most iconic park — prioritize it early in the trip when energy is highest. Check the app for any special June seasonal events.

day_by_day.morning: Take the free hotel shuttle to EPCOT, arriving at rope drop (~9:00 AM). Head immediately to World Discovery to ride Guardians of the Galaxy: Cosmic Rewind (virtual queue — join as soon as the park opens via the app). Then ride Test Track and Mission: SPACE before lines grow.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore World Showcase starting at 11:00 AM — walk the 11 country pavilions around the lagoon. Enjoy free entertainment, cultural exhibits, and street performers. Visit the Mexico Pavilion (ride Gran Fiesta Tour — short wait, air-conditioned). Browse the Norway, Japan, and France pavilions. Look for EPCOT International Food & Wine Festival booths if running (typically starts in July, but check for early June events).
day_by_day.evening: Stay for EPCOT Forever or Harmonious nighttime spectacular over World Showcase Lagoon (check app for timing). Find a spot near the International Gateway for a great view. Shuttle back to hotel afterward.

meals.breakfast: Hotel room breakfast — instant oatmeal, fruit, and coffee from groceries.
meals.lunch: Sunshine Seasons in The Land Pavilion — one of EPCOT's best budget quick-service spots. Rotisserie chicken, sandwiches, and salads ~$11-14.
meals.dinner: World Showcase food booths or Katsura Grill in the Japan Pavilion — teriyaki chicken bowl ~$13. Alternatively, share a large meal from the France or Morocco pavilion food windows.

day_by_day.notes: EPCOT is very walkable but large — wear comfortable shoes. The World Showcase doesn't open until 11:00 AM, so use the morning for rides in World Discovery and World Nature. Stay hydrated — June in Florida is hot and humid.

day_by_day.morning: Take the hotel shuttle to Hollywood Studios, arriving at rope drop. Make a beeline for Star Wars: Galaxy's Edge — ride Millennium Falcon: Smugglers Run first (shorter wait than Rise of the Resistance). Then immediately join the virtual queue or Individual Lightning Lane for Star Wars: Rise of the Resistance — the most immersive ride in all of Disney World.
day_by_day.afternoon: Ride Slinky Dog Dash and Toy Story Mania in Toy Story Land (great for all ages). Catch the Indiana Jones Epic Stunt Spectacular show (free with park admission, check schedule). Visit the Animation Courtyard and catch Disney Junior Play & Dance if traveling with young kids.
day_by_day.evening: Watch the Fantasmic! nighttime show (check app for showtimes — usually 8:00 or 9:30 PM). Arrive 45 minutes early for good seating. This is a must-see spectacular with minimal extra cost. Shuttle back to hotel after the show.

meals.breakfast: Hotel room breakfast to save money.
meals.lunch: Woody's Lunch Box in Toy Story Land — one of the most affordable and beloved quick-service spots. Grilled cheese, BBQ brisket melts, and totchos ~$10-13.
meals.dinner: Backlot Express near Echo Lake — burgers, chicken strips, and sandwiches ~$11-14. Sit in the air-conditioned interior to cool down before the evening show.

day_by_day.notes: Hollywood Studios has the most in-demand rides at Disney World — arrive early and use the app aggressively. Fantasmic! is free with park admission and absolutely worth staying for. This is a high-energy day, so pace yourself in the afternoon heat.

day_by_day.morning: Take the hotel shuttle to Disney's Animal Kingdom, arriving at rope drop. Head directly to Pandora – The World of Avatar and ride Avatar Flight of Passage (the park's most popular ride — waits can exceed 2 hours by mid-morning). Then ride Na'vi River Journey in the same land.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Africa and ride Kilimanjaro Safaris — best in the morning or late afternoon when animals are most active. Visit the Gorilla Falls Exploration Trail (free walking trail with gorillas, hippos, and exotic birds). Catch the Festival of the Lion King show in Africa — a spectacular live performance included with park admission.
day_by_day.evening: Watch the Rivers of Light nighttime show or Tree of Life Awakenings (the Tree of Life lights up with animal projections after dark — magical and free with admission). Animal Kingdom closes earlier than other parks (~8–9 PM), so plan accordingly. Head back to the hotel and rest — you've earned it!

meals.breakfast: Hotel room breakfast.
meals.lunch: Flame Tree Barbecue in Discovery Island — one of Disney World's best quick-service meals. Ribs, pulled pork, and chicken with beautiful outdoor waterfront seating ~$13-16. Share a platter to save.
meals.dinner: Satu'li Canteen in Pandora — customizable bowls with rice, noodles, or salad base with protein ~$13-15. Healthy, filling, and one of the best quick-service values in all of Disney World.

day_by_day.notes: Animal Kingdom is best experienced in the morning and late afternoon — midday heat is intense and animals retreat to shade. The park is also the most nature-focused, so take time to enjoy the walking trails and live entertainment, which are all included with admission.

day_by_day.morning: Take a well-deserved rest morning — sleep in until 8:00–9:00 AM. Use the hotel pool to cool off and relax. This is a great day to do laundry if needed, recharge devices, and review any missed experiences from earlier in the week. Check the My Disney Experience app for any park reservations or Lightning Lane availability.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Disney Springs (FREE admission — no park ticket required). Explore the massive outdoor shopping, dining, and entertainment complex. Browse World of Disney (the largest Disney merchandise store in the world), visit the LEGO Store, and enjoy free street entertainment and live music. Walk along the waterfront and enjoy the atmosphere.
day_by_day.evening: Catch a movie at the AMC Disney Springs 24 theater (~$15-18 per ticket) or enjoy free live music at the Marketplace Stage. Have dinner at one of Disney Springs' more affordable options before heading back to the hotel via the free Disney Springs shuttle.

meals.breakfast: Hotel room breakfast — use remaining groceries from the week.
meals.lunch: Chicken Guy! at Disney Springs — Guy Fieri's chicken tender restaurant with 22 dipping sauces. Tenders and fries ~$12-15. Great value and very popular.
meals.dinner: D-Luxe Burger at Disney Springs — gourmet burgers with creative toppings ~$13-16. Alternatively, grab food from the Marketplace food trucks for ~$10-12 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Disney Springs is completely free to enter and a great way to experience Disney magic without using a park ticket. It's also one of the best spots for souvenir shopping — prices are the same as in the parks but the atmosphere is more relaxed. The free shuttle from the hotel makes this an easy, low-cost day.

day_by_day.morning: Use this final day to revisit your favorite park or catch any missed experiences. If you have a park-hopper ticket, start at Magic Kingdom for a final Main Street stroll and any rides with shorter Sunday morning waits. Alternatively, revisit EPCOT's World Showcase for any pavilions you missed. Pick up last-minute souvenirs — look for discounted items at the end of your trip.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the hotel by 2:00–3:00 PM to pack, check out (or store luggage at the front desk), and freshen up. Take one last dip in the hotel pool if time allows. Confirm your departure transportation — rideshare to Orlando International Airport is ~$25-35 and takes about 30-40 minutes depending on traffic.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Orlando International Airport with plenty of time before your departure flight. Enjoy a final Florida meal at the airport or grab snacks from a convenience store near the hotel before leaving.

meals.breakfast: Final hotel room breakfast — finish any remaining groceries to avoid waste.
meals.lunch: If in a park: Casey's Corner at Magic Kingdom (hot dogs and corn dog nuggets ~$9-12) or a quick-service spot of your choice. If at the hotel: nearby Denny's or IHOP on US-192 for a classic American breakfast/lunch combo (~$10-14 per person).
meals.dinner: Airport dining or a final meal at a budget-friendly restaurant near the hotel such as Olive Garden, Applebee's, or Perkins on US-192 — all within 1-2 miles of the Ramada.

day_by_day.notes: Final day tips: Check the My Disney Experience app for any last-minute Lightning Lane availability. Return any rented strollers or equipment. Take photos on Main Street U.S.A. for a classic Disney farewell. Budget recap: By using the free hotel shuttle daily, eating hotel breakfasts, sharing meals, and refilling water bottles, a family of 4 can save $200-400+ over the week compared to buying everything in-park.

day_by_day.morning: N/A – Flight arrives at 22:30. No morning activities scheduled.
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A – In transit. No afternoon activities scheduled.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Orlando International Airport at 22:30 on United Flight UA. Collect luggage, arrange ground transportation or use the Ramada free theme park shuttle if available at that hour, and check in to Ramada by Wyndham Kissimmee Gateway. Unpack, review the week's park schedule, and get a good night's rest.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or at the airport before departure.
meals.lunch: On the plane or at the airport.
meals.dinner: Grab a quick late-night bite at a nearby 24-hour option such as Denny's or IHOP on W Irlo Bronson Memorial Hwy (both within 1–2 miles of the hotel), or pick up snacks from a nearby Walgreens or Publix to settle in comfortably.

day_by_day.notes: Purchase Disney park tickets online in advance if not already done. Download the My Disney Experience app and link your tickets. Set an early alarm for Day 2 to maximize park time. The hotel offers a free theme park shuttle — check the shuttle schedule at the front desk upon check-in.

day_by_day.morning: Magic Kingdom Park Adventure – Take the hotel's free shuttle to Magic Kingdom. Arrive at rope drop (park typically opens at 9:00 AM). Head straight to Tomorrowland for Space Mountain, then move to Fantasyland for Seven Dwarfs Mine Train and Peter Pan's Flight before crowds build. Use Lightning Lane passes strategically for the most popular rides.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Magic Kingdom. Visit Adventureland for Pirates of the Caribbean and the Jungle Cruise, then head to Liberty Square for the Haunted Mansion. Take a midday break at a shaded area or a sit-down restaurant to recharge during the hottest part of the day (typically 1–3 PM in June).
day_by_day.evening: Stay in Magic Kingdom for the evening spectacular. Watch the 'Disney Enchantment' fireworks show and the Main Street Electrical Parade (check current schedule on the app). Grab a prime viewing spot on Main Street U.S.A. about 30–45 minutes before showtime. Return to the hotel via the free shuttle after the show.

meals.breakfast: Quick breakfast at the hotel or grab a pastry and coffee at Main Street Bakery (Starbucks) inside Magic Kingdom upon arrival.
meals.lunch: Columbia Harbour House in Liberty Square – a mid-range counter-service spot offering clam chowder, fish and chips, and lobster rolls at reasonable prices (~$12–$18 per entrée).
meals.dinner: The Plaza Restaurant on Main Street U.S.A. – a table-service restaurant with classic American comfort food. Make an Advance Dining Reservation (ADR) on the My Disney Experience app. Budget approximately $20–$35 per adult.

day_by_day.notes: June weather in Orlando is hot and humid with afternoon thunderstorms common. Wear light, breathable clothing, apply sunscreen, and carry ponchos. Stay hydrated — free water is available at any quick-service location. Arrive at the park 30 minutes before official opening for the best experience.

day_by_day.morning: Disney's Hollywood Studios – Star Wars Experience. Take the hotel shuttle to Hollywood Studios. Head directly to Star Wars: Galaxy's Edge at park opening. Ride Millennium Falcon: Smugglers Run first (shorter wait early), then join the virtual queue or Lightning Lane for Star Wars: Rise of the Resistance, one of the most immersive rides in all of Disney World.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore more of Hollywood Studios. Visit Toy Story Land for Slinky Dog Dash and Alien Swirling Saucers. Then head to Sunset Boulevard for Rock 'n' Roller Coaster Starring Aerosmith and The Twilight Zone Tower of Terror. Catch the Indiana Jones Epic Stunt Spectacular if timing aligns (check the show schedule on the app).
day_by_day.evening: End the day with the 'Fantasmic!' nighttime show at Hollywood Studios (check current schedule). This spectacular outdoor amphitheater show features Mickey Mouse, beloved Disney characters, and stunning water and fire effects. Arrive 45 minutes early for good seating. Return to the hotel via shuttle.

meals.breakfast: Grab a quick bite at the hotel continental breakfast or stop at Ronto Roasters in Galaxy's Edge for a Ronto Wrap — a unique and delicious park breakfast option (~$13).
meals.lunch: Woody's Lunch Box in Toy Story Land – a fan-favorite counter-service spot with grilled cheese sandwiches, BBQ brisket melts, and totchos (tater tot nachos). Budget ~$10–$15 per person.
meals.dinner: Sci-Fi Dine-In Theater Restaurant – a unique mid-range table-service experience where you dine in retro cars while watching classic sci-fi movie clips. Make an ADR in advance. Budget ~$20–$35 per adult.

day_by_day.notes: Hollywood Studios is one of the busiest parks — arrive early and prioritize Galaxy's Edge. Check the My Disney Experience app for real-time wait times and show schedules. The 'Fantasmic!' dining package is available if you want guaranteed seating for the show.

day_by_day.morning: EPCOT World Showcase & Food Exploration – Take the hotel shuttle to EPCOT. Start in Future World (now called World Discovery and World Nature) and ride Guardians of the Galaxy: Cosmic Rewind (join the virtual queue immediately at park open) and Test Track. Then explore Spaceship Earth, the iconic geodesic sphere.
day_by_day.afternoon: Transition to the World Showcase, which opens at 11:00 AM. Stroll through the 11 international pavilions — Mexico, Norway, China, Germany, Italy, America, Japan, Morocco, France, United Kingdom, and Canada. Ride Frozen Ever After in the Norway Pavilion and Remy's Ratatouille Adventure in the France Pavilion (use Lightning Lane). Sample food and drinks from multiple countries as you walk.
day_by_day.evening: Stay for EPCOT's 'EPCOT Forever' or 'Harmonious' nighttime spectacular over World Showcase Lagoon (verify current show name on the app). Find a spot along the lagoon promenade about 30–40 minutes before showtime. Enjoy the stunning fireworks and illuminated kite displays. Return to the hotel via shuttle.

meals.breakfast: Kringla Bakeri og Kafé in the Norway Pavilion – try a school bread (cardamom bun with custard and coconut) and a coffee. Budget ~$8–$12.
meals.lunch: Graze through the World Showcase! Sample a crepe from France (~$9), a bratwurst from Germany (~$11), and a Kakigori (shaved ice) from Japan (~$7). This 'food tour' approach is a fun and budget-friendly way to experience EPCOT.
meals.dinner: Teppan Edo in the Japan Pavilion – a mid-range hibachi-style table-service restaurant with entertaining chefs cooking at your table. Make an ADR in advance. Budget ~$30–$45 per adult. Alternatively, La Hacienda de San Angel in Mexico for a lakeside dinner with World Showcase views.

day_by_day.notes: EPCOT is the largest Disney park — wear comfortable walking shoes. The World Showcase is perfect for adults and older children. Younger kids may prefer the rides in Future World. Check for any EPCOT festivals happening during your visit (Flower & Garden, Food & Wine, etc.) as they add extra food booths and entertainment.

day_by_day.morning: Disney's Animal Kingdom – Safari & Avatar Experience. Take the hotel shuttle to Animal Kingdom. Arrive at rope drop and head immediately to Pandora – The World of Avatar. Ride Avatar Flight of Passage first (the most popular ride in the park with the longest waits) and then Na'vi River Journey. The immersive bioluminescent world of Pandora is breathtaking.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Africa for the Kilimanjaro Safaris — a 20-minute open-air vehicle tour where you'll see real African wildlife including lions, elephants, giraffes, zebras, and hippos. Then explore the Gorilla Falls Exploration Trail on foot. Visit Asia for Expedition Everest roller coaster and Kali River Rapids (you will get wet — plan accordingly). Check the schedule for the Festival of the Lion King show in Africa.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy the Rivers of Light nighttime show at Animal Kingdom if available (verify on the app, as schedules vary). Alternatively, spend the early evening at the Tree of Life and DinoLand U.S.A. before the park closes (Animal Kingdom typically closes earlier than other parks, around 8–9 PM). Return to the hotel and consider a relaxing swim at the hotel pool.

meals.breakfast: Grab a quick breakfast at the hotel or pick up a pastry at Creature Comforts (Starbucks) near the park entrance.
meals.lunch: Satu'li Canteen in Pandora – one of the best counter-service restaurants in all of Disney World. Try the cheeseburger pods or grain bowls with unique Pandoran ingredients. Budget ~$14–$18 per person.
meals.dinner: Yak & Yeti Restaurant in Asia – a mid-range table-service restaurant with Asian-fusion cuisine including Mandarin chicken, ahi tuna nachos, and dim sum. Make an ADR. Budget ~$20–$35 per adult. Alternatively, use the Yak & Yeti Local Food Cafes for a more budget-friendly counter-service option.

day_by_day.notes: Animal Kingdom is best experienced in the morning when animals are most active on the safari. Bring a change of clothes or a poncho for Kali River Rapids. The park is heavily shaded with lush vegetation, making it slightly more comfortable in the heat than other parks. Check show times for Festival of the Lion King — it's a must-see live performance.

day_by_day.morning: Disney Springs Family Entertainment Day – Sleep in a bit and enjoy a relaxed morning. Have a leisurely breakfast at the hotel. Head to Disney Springs mid-morning (free admission, no park ticket required). Explore the Town Center and Marketplace areas. Browse unique Disney merchandise, visit the LEGO Store, and check out the World of Disney — the largest Disney character merchandise store in the world.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue enjoying Disney Springs. Visit the Splitsville Luxury Lanes for bowling and entertainment (great for families, ~$15–$20 per person per game). Check out the AMC Disney Springs 24 movie theater if anyone wants a cool, air-conditioned break. Explore the Landing and West Side areas. Look for street performers and live entertainment throughout the day.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy dinner and evening entertainment at Disney Springs. Catch a live music performance at one of the outdoor stages (free). Consider visiting the Aerophile — a tethered helium balloon ride offering panoramic views of the Disney World resort (~$25 per adult, ~$20 per child). Return to the hotel for a relaxed evening — pack bags and prepare for the final park day tomorrow.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a nearby local diner on W Irlo Bronson Memorial Hwy for a budget-friendly start to the day.
meals.lunch: D-Luxe Burger at Disney Springs – a mid-range counter-service spot with gourmet burgers, hand-cut fries, and milkshakes. Budget ~$15–$20 per person.
meals.dinner: The Boathouse at Disney Springs – a waterfront mid-range to upscale restaurant with fresh seafood, steaks, and classic American fare. Known for its amphicar tours on the water. Make an ADR. Budget ~$30–$50 per adult. For a more budget-friendly option, try Blaze Fast-Fire'd Pizza (~$10–$14) or Chicken Guy! by Guy Fieri (~$10–$15).

day_by_day.notes: Disney Springs is free to enter and a great way to experience Disney magic without a park ticket. Parking is also free. The Aerophile balloon is weather-dependent and may not operate during thunderstorms. Saturday is typically the busiest day at Disney Springs — arrive early to avoid peak crowds. This is a great day to purchase any remaining souvenirs.

day_by_day.morning: Return to a favorite park or revisit Magic Kingdom for any missed experiences. Alternatively, if the family prefers a relaxed final morning, enjoy the hotel pool, pack remaining luggage, and check out. If returning to a park, use this morning to ride any must-do attractions missed earlier in the week. Magic Kingdom is recommended for a magical final morning — ride classics and enjoy Main Street U.S.A. one last time.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on departure flight time, spend the early afternoon wrapping up park activities or heading back to the hotel to collect luggage. If time allows, stop at a nearby souvenir shop on W Irlo Bronson Memorial Hwy for last-minute gifts at lower prices than inside the parks. Head to Orlando International Airport with plenty of time before your flight.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Orlando. Reflect on an incredible week of Disney magic with the family. Safe travels home!

meals.breakfast: Be Our Guest Restaurant in Magic Kingdom (if returning to the park) for a magical breakfast in the Beast's enchanted castle — make an ADR well in advance. Budget ~$25–$35 per adult. Alternatively, enjoy the hotel's complimentary or on-site breakfast before checkout.
meals.lunch: Casey's Corner on Main Street U.S.A. in Magic Kingdom for classic hot dogs and corn dog nuggets — a quick, affordable, and iconic Disney meal (~$10–$14). Or grab a meal at the airport if heading straight there.
meals.dinner: Airport dining or an in-flight meal depending on departure time.

day_by_day.notes: Check hotel checkout time (typically 11:00 AM) and arrange luggage storage at the front desk if you plan to visit a park before departing. Confirm your return shuttle or transportation to the airport. Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before your flight for airport check-in and security at Orlando International Airport, especially during the busy summer season. Download any Disney photos from PhotoPass before leaving.

experiences.description: Immerse your family in the ultimate Star Wars: Galaxy's Edge experience at Disney's Hollywood Studios. Pilot the Millennium Falcon on Smugglers Run, survive the epic Rise of the Resistance ride, and build your own custom lightsaber at Savi's Workshop. Also enjoy Toy Story Land and the thrilling Tower of Terror for a full day of entertainment.
experiences.location: Disney's Hollywood Studios, Walt Disney World Resort, Lake Buena Vista

experiences.name: Disney Springs Family Entertainment Day
experiences.description: Spend a fun-filled day at Disney Springs, Disney World's free-admission entertainment and shopping district just minutes from Kissimmee. Enjoy live street performances, visit the LEGO Store, dine at world-class restaurants like The Boathouse or T-REX Cafe, and catch a movie at the AMC Disney Springs 24 theater. Great for a budget-friendly family day out.
experiences.location: Disney Springs, Walt Disney World Resort, Lake Buena Vista

experiences.name: Disney's Animal Kingdom Safari & Avatar Experience
experiences.description: Embark on the Kilimanjaro Safaris to see real African wildlife including lions, elephants, and giraffes roaming freely. Then journey to Pandora – The World of Avatar for the awe-inspiring Flight of Passage ride and the Na'vi River Journey. End the day with a live Finding Nemo musical show, making it a perfect blend of nature, culture, and family entertainment.
experiences.location: Disney's Animal Kingdom, Walt Disney World Resort, Lake Buena Vista

day_by_day.morning: N/A – Flight arrives late evening
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A – In transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Orlando International Airport at 22:30 via United Airlines. Take a pre-arranged private car transfer (book through Mears Connect Black or a luxury car service) to Ramada by Wyndham Kissimmee Gateway. Check in, unpack, and settle into your room. Grab a light late-night snack from a nearby 24-hour convenience store or hotel vending area.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or at the airport before departure
meals.lunch: On the plane or at the airport
meals.dinner: Late-night arrival – grab a light snack at the hotel or order room service / delivery via DoorDash from a nearby restaurant such as Perkins Restaurant & Bakery (open late, 5 min drive)

day_by_day.notes: Do not schedule any theme park activities today. Prioritize rest as Day 2 will be a full park day. Confirm your Disney park reservations and Lightning Lane Multi Pass purchases via the My Disney Experience app before sleeping. Lay out comfortable walking shoes and park essentials for the morning.

day_by_day.morning: Rise early and take the hotel's free theme park shuttle to Magic Kingdom Park (first shuttle typically departs around 7:30–8:00 AM). Arrive at rope drop (park opens ~9:00 AM) to maximize time. Begin with Tomorrowland – ride Space Mountain and TRON Lightcycle / Run using Lightning Lane Individual selections booked in advance. Move to Fantasyland for Seven Dwarfs Mine Train early before crowds build.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Adventureland – experience Pirates of the Caribbean and Jungle Cruise. Enjoy a leisurely lunch at Be Our Guest Restaurant in Fantasyland (prix-fixe lunch, book well in advance). After lunch, head to Liberty Square for the Haunted Mansion, then Frontierland for Big Thunder Mountain Railroad. Use Lightning Lane Multi Pass strategically throughout the afternoon to minimize wait times.
day_by_day.evening: Secure a prime viewing spot on Main Street U.S.A. for the Disney Enchantment fireworks spectacular (typically 9:00 PM). Before the show, enjoy dinner at Cinderella's Royal Table inside Cinderella Castle – a signature dining experience requiring advance reservations. After fireworks, take the hotel shuttle back and wind down.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the hotel or grab a quick bite at Main Street Bakery (Starbucks) inside Magic Kingdom upon arrival
meals.lunch: Be Our Guest Restaurant – prix-fixe French-inspired menu inside Beast's Castle, Fantasyland (~$65–$80/adult)
meals.dinner: Cinderella's Royal Table – signature two-story castle dining with character meet-and-greets, prix-fixe menu (~$85–$115/adult). Book 60 days in advance.

day_by_day.notes: Purchase Lightning Lane Multi Pass ($25–$35/person/day) and individual Lightning Lane selections for TRON and Seven Dwarfs Mine Train at 7:00 AM sharp via the app. Wear sunscreen and bring a portable fan – June in Orlando is hot and humid (expect 90°F+). Stay hydrated throughout the day.

day_by_day.morning: Take the hotel shuttle to EPCOT for rope drop. Begin in World Discovery – ride Guardians of the Galaxy: Cosmic Rewind (virtual queue or Lightning Lane Individual – book at 7:00 AM). Then experience Test Track and Mission: SPACE (Green Mission for families, Orange for thrill-seekers). Move to World Nature to explore The Seas with Nemo & Friends and Soarin' Around the World.
day_by_day.afternoon: Transition into the World Showcase, which opens at 11:00 AM. Begin your international culinary journey – start in Mexico at La Hacienda de San Angel for a lakeside lunch. Stroll through Morocco, France, Japan, and Italy pavilions, sampling street food and artisan goods. Catch a live cultural performance or film presentation in the Canada or France pavilions. Visit the newly expanded World Showcase pavilions and browse premium merchandise.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a premium dinner at Monsieur Paul, EPCOT's acclaimed French fine-dining restaurant above the France Pavilion, offering an exquisite prix-fixe menu with panoramic lagoon views. After dinner, secure a lakeside spot for EPCOT Forever or Luminous The Symphony of Us nighttime spectacular over World Showcase Lagoon. Return via hotel shuttle.

meals.breakfast: Grab a croissant and café au lait at Les Halles Boulangerie-Patisserie in the France Pavilion upon arrival
meals.lunch: La Hacienda de San Angel – upscale Mexican cuisine with lagoon views in the Mexico Pavilion (~$40–$60/adult)
meals.dinner: Monsieur Paul – AAA Four Diamond French fine dining, prix-fixe menu (~$120–$160/adult). Advance reservations essential.

day_by_day.notes: EPCOT's International Food & Wine Festival may be running in June – check Disney's calendar for special kiosks and celebrity chef events which add incredible value. Wear comfortable shoes as World Showcase is a 1.3-mile loop. Consider renting a stroller for young children.

day_by_day.morning: Take the hotel shuttle to Disney's Hollywood Studios for rope drop. Head immediately to Star Wars: Galaxy's Edge – ride Millennium Falcon: Smugglers Run first (shorter morning wait), then secure a boarding group or Lightning Lane for Star Wars: Rise of the Resistance, the most immersive ride in Walt Disney World. Explore Black Spire Outpost, build a custom lightsaber at Savi's Workshop (premium experience, ~$250/lightsaber, book in advance), or create a custom droid at the Droid Depot.
day_by_day.afternoon: Experience Toy Story Land – ride Slinky Dog Dash and Alien Swirling Saucers. Then head to Sunset Boulevard for The Twilight Zone Tower of Terror and Rock 'n' Roller Coaster Starring Aerosmith. Catch the Indiana Jones Epic Stunt Spectacular show (check daily schedule). Enjoy a mid-afternoon lunch at Sci-Fi Dine-In Theater Restaurant – a unique drive-in movie themed dining experience.
day_by_day.evening: Experience the Fantasmic! nighttime spectacular at the Hollywood Hills Amphitheater (check show times – typically two shows on busy nights). Book the Fantasmic! Dining Package at Hollywood & Vine or Mama Melrose's for guaranteed reserved seating. After the show, browse Star Wars merchandise at the Dok-Ondar's Den of Antiquities before heading back to the hotel.

meals.breakfast: Ronto Roasters in Galaxy's Edge – try the Ronto Morning Wrap, a beloved park breakfast item with a Star Wars twist
meals.lunch: Sci-Fi Dine-In Theater Restaurant – American comfort food in a retro drive-in setting with classic sci-fi film clips (~$35–$55/adult)
meals.dinner: Oga's Cantina for themed cocktails and appetizers (reservations required, 45-min limit), followed by dinner at Docking Bay 7 Food and Cargo for a more substantial Star Wars-themed meal

day_by_day.notes: Savi's Workshop lightsaber building experience (~$250 per lightsaber) must be booked well in advance and is a once-in-a-lifetime premium experience highly recommended for Star Wars fans of all ages. Galaxy's Edge is best experienced early morning or late evening when crowds thin. Download the Play Disney Parks app for interactive Galaxy's Edge missions.

day_by_day.morning: Enjoy a relaxed morning – sleep in and have a leisurely breakfast. This is your recovery and resort day. Visit the hotel pool or arrange a morning spa treatment at a nearby luxury spa (The Spa at Four Seasons Orlando is a 10-minute drive and offers world-class treatments). Alternatively, take a short drive to Disney's BoardWalk area for a scenic morning stroll along the waterfront promenade.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Disney Springs for the afternoon – the hotel shuttle may service this area, or take a rideshare (10-minute drive). Explore the four neighborhoods: The Landing, Marketplace, Town Center, and West Side. Browse premium retailers including UNIQLO, Anthropologie, and the massive World of Disney store. Visit the LEGO Store, Art of Disney gallery, and Splitsville Luxury Lanes for bowling. Catch a movie at the AMC Disney Springs 24 if desired.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a premium dinner at STK Orlando at Disney Springs – a modern steakhouse with a vibrant atmosphere offering USDA prime cuts and an extensive wine list. After dinner, explore the entertainment district – catch a live performance at the House of Blues or enjoy cocktails at Jock Lindsey's Hangar Bar with its Indiana Jones theming. Return to the hotel via shuttle or rideshare.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely hotel breakfast or visit First Watch (5-min drive from hotel) for a premium brunch experience
meals.lunch: Lunch at The BOATHOUSE at Disney Springs – upscale waterfront dining featuring fresh seafood, prime steaks, and dream boats (~$45–$70/adult)
meals.dinner: STK Orlando – modern American steakhouse with USDA prime cuts, craft cocktails, and DJ entertainment (~$80–$130/adult). Reservations recommended.

day_by_day.notes: Disney Springs is free admission – no park ticket required. This is an ideal day to recharge before the final two park days. Use this time to review your Lightning Lane bookings and dining reservations for the remaining days. Consider purchasing any remaining Disney souvenirs or gifts here as selection is vast and prices are consistent with the parks.

day_by_day.morning: Take the hotel shuttle to Disney's Animal Kingdom for rope drop. Begin with Pandora – The World of Avatar: ride Avatar Flight of Passage immediately at rope drop (this is the most in-demand ride in all of Walt Disney World – Lightning Lane Individual purchase at 7:00 AM is strongly recommended). Follow with Na'vi River Journey for a serene boat ride through bioluminescent rainforest. Explore the Valley of Mo'ara and take photos of the floating Hallelujah Mountains.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Africa for the Kilimanjaro Safaris – book a late morning or early afternoon time for the best wildlife activity (animals are more active in cooler parts of the day). See lions, elephants, giraffes, hippos, and more in a stunning open-air savanna setting. Explore the Gorilla Falls Exploration Trail on foot. Visit Asia for Expedition Everest – Legend of the Forbidden Mountain and Kali River Rapids (bring a change of clothes or a poncho). Enjoy lunch at Tiffins Restaurant, Animal Kingdom's premier fine-dining establishment.
day_by_day.evening: Experience the Rivers of Light: We Are One nighttime spectacular at the Discovery River Amphitheater (check show schedule). Before the show, enjoy the Tree of Life Awakenings – the iconic 145-foot tree comes alive with projected animal stories after dark. Dine at Tiffins for dinner (if not used for lunch) or enjoy cocktails at Nomad Lounge. Return to the hotel via shuttle.

meals.breakfast: Grab a Pongu Pongu drink and a snack at the Pandora – World of Avatar area, or eat at the hotel before departure
meals.lunch: Tiffins Restaurant – Animal Kingdom's AAA Four Diamond signature restaurant featuring globally-inspired cuisine with stunning artwork (~$55–$85/adult). Book 60 days in advance.
meals.dinner: Nomad Lounge (adjacent to Tiffins) for artisan cocktails and small plates, or a full dinner at Tiffins if reserved for the evening

day_by_day.notes: Saturday is typically one of the busiest days at Disney World – arrive at rope drop without exception. Lightning Lane Multi Pass and Individual selections are critical today. Avatar Flight of Passage is a must-do and sells out quickly. Bring ponchos for Kali River Rapids. Animal Kingdom typically closes earlier than other parks (~8:00–9:00 PM), so plan accordingly.

day_by_day.morning: For your final full day, return to your favorite park or split the day between two parks using the Park Hopper option (if purchased). Recommended: revisit Magic Kingdom for any missed attractions or to re-experience favorites. Alternatively, return to EPCOT for any World Showcase pavilions not fully explored. Use the morning for any remaining Lightning Lane experiences and collect final souvenirs from the parks.
day_by_day.afternoon: Enjoy a special farewell lunch at one of Disney World's most iconic restaurants. Consider Victoria & Albert's at Disney's Grand Floridian Resort & Spa – the only AAA Five Diamond restaurant in all of Florida and one of the finest dining experiences in the United States (jacket required for gentlemen, prix-fixe only, ~$295–$385/adult). Alternatively, enjoy a character dining farewell lunch at 1900 Park Fare at the Grand Floridian for a more family-friendly premium experience. After lunch, take a monorail ride around the Seven Seas Lagoon for stunning resort views.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the hotel by early evening to begin packing and preparing for departure. Enjoy a final dinner at a nearby upscale Kissimmee restaurant – Capa Steakhouse at the Four Seasons Orlando (10-min drive) is an exceptional rooftop steakhouse with views of Magic Kingdom fireworks. After dinner, return to the hotel, complete packing, and arrange your departure transportation. Reflect on an unforgettable Disney World luxury experience.

meals.breakfast: Final hotel breakfast or a special treat at Amorette's Patisserie at Disney Springs for artisan pastries and custom cakes
meals.lunch: Victoria & Albert's at Disney's Grand Floridian Resort – Florida's only AAA Five Diamond restaurant, prix-fixe tasting menu (~$295–$385/adult, wine pairing available). Book 60 days in advance. OR 1900 Park Fare character dining (~$55–$75/adult) for a family-friendly alternative.
meals.dinner: Capa Steakhouse at Four Seasons Orlando – rooftop Spanish-inspired steakhouse with Magic Kingdom fireworks views (~$90–$140/adult). Reservations essential.

day_by_day.notes: Victoria & Albert's requires reservations exactly 60 days in advance and is one of the hardest reservations to secure in all of Disney World – book the moment your 60-day window opens. If unavailable, Narcoossee's at the Grand Floridian (waterfront seafood, ~$70–$100/adult) is an excellent alternative with fireworks views. Confirm your departure transportation the night before. The hotel's free shuttle may not run early enough for morning flights – arrange a private car service if needed.

query: Disney World Orlando family of 4, $6000, 7 days, June
